🚀 Welcome to NovaLoop!

We are a team interested in space, science, and technology. Our project, MISSION REPLAY: LIFELOOP, is an interactive game exploring how humans could manage resources and sustain life on Mars.

We're looking for creative and motivated members interested in coding, game development, design, science, and space exploration.

📩 Team Contact: novaloop.team@gmail.com
summary:
LIFELOOP is an integrated sustainable settlement concept designed to explore how humans could live on Mars by connecting essential life-support systems. The project brings together oxygen production, water recovery, food production, algae-based biological systems, solar energy, radiation protection, waste management, and crew safety.
We developed a 3D interactive educational prototype that allows users to explore the settlement and make strategic decisions about its resources. Players must balance oxygen, water, energy, and food while managing different colony systems. Each decision has consequences that can affect the settlement during later mission days. Players can also explore different starting scenarios and compare the outcomes of their decisions.
Inspired by NASA research and resources, LIFELOOP aims to help people understand the scientific and engineering challenges of creating a sustainable human settlement beyond Earth.
details:
Project Overview
LIFELOOP is a proposed integrated settlement concept designed to explore the challenges of supporting human life on Mars. Living on Mars requires more than building habitats. A sustainable settlement must manage limited resources and connect several systems that depend on one another.
Our concept brings these systems together into one settlement. The 3D game is an educational prototype that demonstrates some of the main interactions and resource-management challenges.
Main Systems
1. Oxygen Production
The oxygen system is inspired by NASA's MOXIE experiment, which demonstrated the production of oxygen from carbon dioxide in the Martian atmosphere. LIFELOOP includes an oxygen station to represent the importance of producing and managing oxygen for the crew.
2. Water Recovery
Water is an essential resource for drinking, hygiene, and growing plants. The settlement includes a water recovery and recycling system to demonstrate why water conservation is important when supplies are limited.
3. Food Production
The proposed settlement includes a controlled-environment greenhouse using hydroponic growing methods. Its crop plan includes potatoes, lettuce, kale, herbs, dwarf wheat, and tomatoes. The design also considers growing media such as LECA.
The proposed crop allocation is 160 square meters:
Potatoes: 40 m²
Dwarf wheat: 35 m²
Tomatoes: 25 m²
Lettuce: 25 m²
Kale: 20 m²
Herbs: 15 m²
These values represent a proposed design, not a scientifically validated guarantee of food production for the crew. In the current game prototype, users can interact with five crop options: potatoes, tomatoes, lettuce, dwarf wheat, and kale.
4. Algae-Based Biological System
The concept includes a bioreactor using Spirulina and Chlorella. These algae use light, water, nutrients, and carbon dioxide during photosynthesis and release oxygen. Their possible role in food-related production also requires controlled cultivation and safety evaluation.
5. Solar Energy
Solar panels provide an important energy source for the settlement. Energy is needed by life-support equipment, water systems, greenhouse lighting, and other facilities. The game demonstrates why energy must be managed carefully.
6. Radiation Protection and Crew Safety
The settlement concept includes protected habitats with thick regolith-covered roofs to represent radiation shielding. It also includes crew facilities and healthcare-related spaces to support human safety and well-being.
6. Waste Management and Recycling
Waste management is included as part of the wider settlement design. Recycling and resource recovery can reduce the need to transport new supplies from Earth.
How the Prototype Works
The user explores a 3D Martian settlement and visits five main interactive stations: oxygen, water, greenhouse, solar energy, and algae.

At each station, the user chooses between two strategies. These choices affect available resources immediately, and some decisions create delayed effects during later mission days.
The game tracks three main resources: oxygen, water, and energy. Food reserves are displayed separately. Planting crops uses water and energy while improving the food reserve.
Each playthrough begins with one of four starting scenarios, so the initial resource conditions can differ. Users can replay the mission and try different strategies to explore how their decisions affect the final colony condition.
Educational Value and Importance
LIFELOOP helps users understand that a Mars settlement cannot depend on one system alone. Oxygen, water, food, energy, and crew safety are connected. A decision that helps one system may create a challenge for another.
The prototype turns these relationships into interactive decisions, helping users explore resource scarcity, sustainability, and the importance of planning in space exploration.
Tools and Technologies
HTML
CSS
JavaScript
Three.js for the 3D environment
NASA scientific resources and data references
Visual Studio Code and a local development server during development
Limitations
The current prototype is an educational model, not a complete scientific simulation of Mars. Resource values, daily consumption, scenario conditions, and decision consequences are simplified gameplay mechanics. They are not direct NASA measurements or validated engineering predictions.
The wider LIFELOOP concept includes additional systems and design ideas that are not all fully interactive in the current prototype.

7 Hardware and Software
Software:
HTML, CSS, and JavaScript for developing the game.
Three.js for creating the 3D interactive environment.
Visual Studio Code for writing and editing the code.
A local development server (Live Server) to run the project during development.
NASA DONKI API for retrieving space-weather information.
Hardware:
A computer or laptop was used for developing and running the project.

Use of Super Intelligence (SI):

We used Google AI as an assisting tool during the development process. It helped us organize and improve written explanations, understand scientific and technical information and we used Canva to edit the project video and add background music.

The project idea, its main purpose, and the selection of the settlement systems were developed by our team. AI was used as a supporting tool to help us work on and communicate our own concept.
